_activity: Watch one get built: the Bridgewater Canal, 1761
intro: Nothing to answer here. This one is already done, so you can see what it looks like built.

left.label: In 1761, the Bridgewater Canal began carrying coal from the mines at Worsley to Manchester, and by 1762 the price of coal in Manchester had fallen by about half (Doc 9).

right.label: This shows moving coal by water cost far less than moving it by road, which matters because cheap fuel helped Manchester grow into a mill town.

rationale.a: The first half says what the evidence shows, in your own words. “Which matters because” is the so what: why it mattered to Britain's factories. Notice it never repeats the price numbers.

frame_fill: This shows moving coal by water cost far less than moving it by road, which matters because cheap fuel helped Manchester grow into a mill town.

documents.source_text: The Bridgewater Canal opened in 1761. It carried coal about 10 miles from the mines at Worsley to Manchester. One horse could pull a canal boat carrying about 30 tons, more than ten times what a horse and cart could carry. By 1762, the price of coal in Manchester had fallen by about half.
